Hi Jane — thanks for the clear questions. High-level answers below and an attached starter sample list (ACME_Sample_Control_List.xlsx).

1) Sampling window
- FedRAMP: auditors commonly ask for at least 90 consecutive days of logs for AU controls, and evidence of continuous operation for 12 months for some CM/IA controls depending on high-impact mapping. For a readiness assessment we usually provide a 90-day export and call out any 12-month artifacts separately.
- ISO 27001: surveillance audits usually look for evidence over the last 6–12 months for management review and continual improvement records; operational controls commonly reviewed over the most recent 3–6 months.

2) Artifact formats
- Preferred: single exports (CSV/JSON/PDF) from the system for logs and access lists; signed policy PDFs for documentation; system configuration snapshots (exported JSON/YAML) for CM controls.
- Acceptable: screenshots with clear timestamps + export where exports are not available.

3) Sample sizes and selection approach
- Privileged access reviews: sample 5–10 users across critical services OR full export of privileged accounts if under 50.
- Change management: 10–15 change tickets spanning low/medium/high risk in the sampling window; include approvals and rollback notes.
- Configuration drift: 5 representative instances per service (more for high-impact services).

Next steps / proposed mutual action plan (owners & tentative dates):
- Laura (Acme) to confirm system owners and priority systems by 2027-03-24 (owner: Jane)
- Redwood to deliver final sample control list + extraction guidance by 2027-03-26 (owner: Lauren) — attached

- Redwood to run a dry-run evidence ingest and sanity check by 2027-04-08 (owner: Marcus Lin)

I attached a starter checklist. Marcus and Soojin are copied to help with export formats and a short validation script we can run. If the audit team prefers a 12-month window for specific controls we can note that in the plan and escalate resource needs.

Thanks — a couple of clarifications from the runtime/infra side: 

- Logs: we can provide raw token-level access logs and node-level system logs. For AU auditability we recommend a 90-day export in compressed JSONL plus a weekly rolling export for continuity. If FedRAMP wants 12 months for specific controls we can provide a summary + hashes for older logs (to avoid moving multi-TB datasets).
- Retention: default platform retention for debug logs is 90 days; audit/security logs are retained 12 months for Dedicated/Private customers. If Acme is on Hosted, we can offer a one-off 12-month export under an evidence request (need 5 business days).
- Change tickets: please include ticket IDs, diff snapshots, approval records, and deployment timestamps. If you can't export diffs, include before/after config snapshots.

Quick ask: Jane, please indicate whether Acme needs the longer 12-month exports for the readiness assessment or only for production FedRAMP baseline. That will change the extraction timeline.

Marcus Lin
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
